content:
mike: FYI we just got a 3rd-party escalation — tenant `acme-inc` is seeing lots of 502/504s and timeouts hitting our hosted inference API since ~09:10 UTC. Customer says spikes correlate with batch jobs they started.
sasha: digging. can you paste sample request ids or x-request headers? any pattern on model or route?
mike: customer provided a few request ids: r_8f3a2, r_8f3a9, r_8f3b0. All to /v1/generate on model `rw-large-v2`. They say tail latency shoots to 30s+ then gateway 504.
tara: opening runtime dashboard now. initial glance: there's a sustained increase in queue depth for the hosted route, continuous batching backlog shows long-lived entries. looks like head-of-line blocking from a few very long token sequences.
noah: customer reports they submitted many long-prompt generations in a tight loop (their internal job) — each request ~2k tokens. they didn't set client-side rate limits.
sasha: that will absolutely amplify KV cache churn + longer decode time -> increases batch latency. our current queue_depth_limit is 128 per route; hitting that means we start rejecting with 429 or queue-timeout 504 depending on config.
mike: customer saw both 5xx and 504s, also intermittent 502s. billing flagged request spikes but no immediate billing break (yet).
pp_support: created support ticket INC-2026 and escalated to eng-runtime. attaching logs from support: ```
[09:12:03] r_8f3a2 route=/v1/generate model=rw-large-v2 queue_depth=127 batch_size=16 latency_ms=31250 status=timeout
[09:12:07] r_8f3a9 route=/v1/generate model=rw-large-v2 queue_depth=128 batch_size=20 status=reject
[09:13:01] r_8f3b0 route=/v1/generate model=rw-large-v2 queue_depth=130 action=overflow status=504
```
sasha: ok thats consistent. hypothesis: continuous batching backlog + several long-sequence requests pushed effective queue depth above safe threshold; batcher cannot drain quickly -> tail latency. we need quick mitigation and a longer-term fix.
tara: immediate mitigations we can do: 1) temporarily lower per-tenant concurrency/queue allowance for acme-inc; 2) enable early-reject policy (reject_at_queue_depth=100) for that route; 3) route their requests to a smaller model (rw-medium) as an automatic fallback; 4) apply a short-lived retry-to-smaller-model in gateway. any objections?
mike: customer will accept fallback to smaller model for now, they prefer availability over fidelity. they asked for repro steps so they can test after change.
sasha: i'll implement 2) and 3) now. @deploy-bot can you create a config patch to set reject_at_queue_depth=100 for tenant acme-inc on /v1/generate and add fallback model `rw-medium`? tag: hotfix-179988.
deploy-bot: config patch created: hotfix-179988, review by tara required.
tara: reviewing. also do we want to instrument and expose `x-request-queue-depth` and `x-batch-latency-ms` in response headers to help customers debug?
noah: that would be helpful to them. they asked for those headers in the ticket.
sasha: agreed, but that's a medium-term change — need API contract review. for now we'll add internal debugging headers in logs.
tara: rolling hotfix  — applying reject_at_queue_depth=100 for acme-inc and adding routing override to prefer rw-medium for requests where header `x-acme-fallback: true` or when queue_depth > 90. will rollout to 15% then 100% in 2 mins.
deploy-bot: hotfix-179988 rolled to 15% at 09:27 UTC. health checks green.
mike: customer pinged — latency is dropping for a subset of requests but still seeing some 504s.
sasha: we need to check if there are in-flight long requests still occupying slots. will patch to decrement batch size upper bound for that route (max_batch_size=8) to reduce queue formation.
tara: lowering max_batch_size to 8 and enabling eager-kv-cache-eviction for rw-large-v2 for acme-inc. applying now.
deploy-bot: config updated, rolled to 100% at 09:31 UTC.
sasha: monitoring... queue depth metrics trending down from 130 -> 40 over ~6 min. 5xxs have dropped significantly.
mike: customer confirms fewer 504s and overall improved throughput. they asked about concrete root cause and next steps.
pp_support: customer followup note added to INC-2026: temporary fallback enabled, queue limits reduced, long-running job guidance sent.
noah: recommend we schedule a consult with acme-inc to help them batch client-side or add jitter and token limits. they will likely want to move to Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput.
sasha: agree. post-incident actions: 1) add per-tenant queue depth metrics and alert when >75% sustained for 2min, 2) add auto-fallback policy that routes to smaller-compatible model when queue_depth > threshold, 3) implement header `x-request-queue-depth` for visibility, 4) evaluate default queue_depth_limit per plan (free vs enterprise).
tara: also add a safety circuit-breaker in the batching pipeline: if avg_batch_latency > 3s and queue_depth > threshold, slow down intake (backpressure to gateway) instead of accumulating more requests.
mike: can we also check whether billing usage spike was accurate? billing-bot, any anomalies?
billing-bot: noticed spike in token usage for acme-inc between 09:10-09:40 UTC. no duplicate charge events. flagged for review under BILL-872.
pp_support: adding all artifacts to INC-2026: logs, metrics links, hotfix diff, customer convo, and recommended follow-ups.
sasha: thanks team. closing loop with customer stating we applied temp mitigations + scheduled later follow-up. will draft postmortem with timeline and impact numbers (requests rejected, 5xx count, duration).
mike: customer grateful and scheduling onboarding call for Dedicated. closing thread for now, will reopen if new 5xxs appear. :thumbsup:
